Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:11:1.hebrew: דנין אותו איצטריכא ליה - סלקא דעתך אמינא: לא ליזלזל למיתי קמי בי דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:11:1.english: It was necessary for [the mishna to state]: "They judge him" - You might have thought to say: He should not be demeaned [by having] to come before the court.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:12:1.hebrew: ועובר על עשה - לקמן פריך: לא סגי דלא עבר?:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:12:1.english: And he transgresses a positive mitzva - Further on, [the Gemara] challenges: Is it not possible that he does not transgress?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:12:2.english: And he is like an ordinary [person] - Further on, it is properly explained.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:1:1.hebrew: מאתים ושבעים ושבעה - מאתים ושלשים כרבי נחמיה, ועוד מ"ז, שאם יתחלקו ב"ד: י"א מזכין ואחד עשר מחייבין, ואחד אומר "איני יודע" — יוסיפו מאלו מ"ז עד שבעים, כדאמרי' בהיו בודקין (לקמן סנהדרין דף מ.): שמוסיפין שנים על הכ"ג. אם יזכוהו שניהם — הרי י"ג מזכין ואחד עשר מחייבין, זכאי; ואם יחייבוהו — חייב, דאיכא הטייה לרעה על פי שנים; ואם יחלקו — צריך עוד להוסיף שנים. וכן לעולם, עד שיהיו שבעים לרבי יהודה, ושבעים ואחד לרבנן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:1:1.english: Two hundred and seventy-seven - Two hundred and thirty in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Nechemya, and an additional forty-seven, so that if the court is divided — eleven acquitting and eleven convicting, and one saying, “I do not know” — they will add from these forty-seven up to seventy, as we say in the chapter entitled “Hayu Vodekin” (below, Sanhedrin 40a): that they add two to the twenty-three. If both of them acquit him, behold there are thirteen acquitting and eleven convicting, and he is acquitted; and if they convict him, he is convicted, for there is an inclination toward guilt by a majority of two; and if they divide, they must add two more. And so on continuously, until there are seventy according to Rabbi Yehuda, and seventy-one according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:3:1.hebrew: שרי אלפים שש מאות - היו, שהרי שש מאות אלף רגלי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:3:1.english: Ministers of thousands [were] six hundred - [There] were, as [there were] six hundred thousand on foot.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:6:1.hebrew: כהן גדול. אינו יוצא אחר המטה - דילמא אתא למינגע. והיינו דאזהר קרא: "ומן המקדש לא יצא" — מקדושתו לא יצא; כלומר, יתרחק מן הכיעור, שלא יבא לידי טומאה. והאי קרא בכה"ג אונן כתיב, דכתיב לעיל מיניה: "לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:6:1.english: A High Priest. He does not follow the bier - Lest he come to touch [it]. And this is what the verse warned: "Neither shall he go out of the Sanctuary" — he shall not go out from his sanctity; that is to say, he must distance himself from what is unseemly, so that he does not come to ritual impurity. And this verse is written regarding a High Priest [who is an] onen [a mourner prior to burial], as it is written before it: "He shall not defile himself for his father or for his mother."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:6:2.hebrew: הן נכסין והוא נגלה - כשהן יוצאין ממבוי זה ונכנסין למבוי אחר, ונכסין ממבוי הראשון שאינו רואה אותן — הוא נגלה ונכנס למבוי הראשון; והן נכסין ממבוי השני — והוא נגלה ונכנס לתוכו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:6:2.english: They are concealed and he is revealed - When they exit this alleyway and enter another alleyway, and are concealed from the first alleyway so that he does not see them, he is revealed and enters the first alleyway; and [when] they are concealed from the second alleyway, he is revealed and enters into it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:7:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda - Interprets “from the Temple” literally.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:1.hebrew: וכשהוא מנחם - בשורה, כשחוזרין מקבור את המת שאין שלו — דרך כל העם עוברין זה אחר זה, ומנחמין את האבל שעומד במעמדו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:1.english: And when he consoles - In the line [of comforters], when they return from burying a deceased person who is not his [relative], the way of all the people is [that] they pass by one after another and console the mourner, who stands in his place.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:2.hebrew: והממונה - סגן הכהנים. ממצעו לכהן גדול בינו לבין העם — שהממונה בימינו, וכל העם בשמאלו, והוא באמצע:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:2.english: And the appointed one - The Deputy High Priest. [He] places the High Priest in the middle, between himself and the people — as the appointed one is on his right, and all the people are on his left, and he [the High Priest] is in the middle.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:3.hebrew: אנו כפרתך - בנו תתכפר אתה, ואנחנו תחתיך לכל הראוי לבא עליך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:3.english: We are your atonement - May you be atoned for through us, and [may] we be in your place for whatever is fitting to come upon you.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:4.hebrew: וכשמברין אותו - כדקיימא לן (במו"ק דף כז:), אבל סעודה ראשונה אסור לאכול משלו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:4.english: And when they provide him the meal of comfort - As is established for us (in Moed Katan 27b), a mourner is forbidden to eat of his own [food] for the first meal.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:5.hebrew: מסובין על הארץ - הן מצירין ומתאבלין על צערו, והוא מיסב בכבוד על הספסל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 18a:8:5.english: Recline on the ground - They grieve and mourn over his sorrow, while he reclines with honor on the bench.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:11:1.hebrew: כהן גדול דן פשיטא - כלומר: למה לי למיתני "דן"? ומשני: "דנין" איצטריכא ליה, דס"ד דמתוך גדולתו אין דנין אותו, ו"דן" קתני אגב "דנין". ופריך: "הא נמי פשיטא!" כלומר: כיון דפשיטא לן דדן, פשיטא נמי דדנין, דאי לאו דדנין וכו'. ולא משני: דסד"א דאין דנין אותו, ומתוך שאין דנין אותו הוא אינו דן — משום דאכתי הוה פריך ליה: ליתני "דן" לבד, ומינה ידעינן דדנין אותו. ומיהו קשה: גבי מלך ליתני "לא דנין", וידעינן שפיר דאינו דן משום "התקוששו"? וי"ל: דלא דמי, דודאי גבי כהן, כיון דתנא "דן", לא הוה ליה למתני "דנין" בחנם; אבל גבי מלך, אין קושיא אמאי קתני "לא דן", כיון דתנא ליה מקמי "לא דנין". ועוד, אגב דתני כהן גדול "דן" ו"דנין", תנא גבי מלך תרווייהו: "לא דן" ו"לא דנין", דהכי נמי קתני "מעידין אותו" גבי כהן גדול, ו"לא מעידין" גבי מלך, אע"ג דלא צריכי, דבכלל "דנין אותו", אלא משום דתנא גבי "דן" — "דנין", תנא נמי "מעיד" ו"מעידים". והא דלא שקיל וטרי בהש"ס הכי, משום דהא פשיטא דתני בסיפא אגב רישא. כך מצאתי בפרישה, הר"ר טרויי"ש בשמו. ובחנם דחק לדקדק כך, דודאי לעולם, בין גבי מלך בין גבי כהן גדול, אי יש חידוש או מ"דן" או מ"דנין", אין להקשות שום דבר: דלמה לו למיתני גבי כהן גדול "דנין אותו", וגבי מלך "לא דן"? דכיון דיש שום חידוש במילתיה, תני זה אגב זה. ותדע דהכי פשיטא ליה להש"ס, דפריך הכא "פשיטא", כלומר: למה לן למתני "דן"? ומשני: "דנין אותו" איצטריכא ליה, ואגב "דנין אותו" תני "דן". אפ"ה אין להקשות: אמאי לא משני דמשום הכי תני "דן" ו"דנין אותו", משום דאי לא תני שום דבר הוה סלקא דעתך דאין דנין אותו, ומתוך כך אינו דן משום "התקוששו"? דאדרבה, לאידך גיסא: אי לא הוה תני שום דבר בכ"ג, הוה אמינא מסברא דדן שפיר, דאטו משום חשיבותו מגרע גרע?! וכיון דדן, איהו נמי דיינינן ליה משום "התקוששו", ולא קשיא מידי:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:11:1.english: "The High Priest judges: [Isn't that] obvious?" - That is to say: Why do I need [the Mishnah] to teach "he judges"? And [the Gemara] answers: It was necessary [for the Mishnah to teach that others] "judge him," for it might enter your mind [to think] that on account of his greatness others do not judge him; and it taught "he judges" alongside "others judge him." And [the Gemara] objects: "This is also obvious!" That is to say: Since it is obvious to us that he judges, it is also obvious that others judge him, for if they do not judge him, etc. [how could he judge, as it is written: "Gather yourselves together and gather", meaning: adorn yourself first, and then adorn others?] And [the Gemara] does not answer that it might enter your mind [to think] that others do not judge him, and because others do not judge him he [too] does not judge — because [the Gemara] would still have objected to it: Let [the Mishnah] teach "he judges" alone, and from that we would know that others judge him! However, there is a difficulty: Regarding a king, let [the Mishnah] teach "others do not judge [him]," and we would well know that he does not judge on account of "Gather yourselves together"? And it can be answered that they are not comparable: for certainly regarding the [High] Priest, since [the Tanna] taught "he judges," he should not have taught "others judge him" gratuitously; but regarding a king, there is no question as to why he teaches "he does not judge," since he taught it before "others do not judge him." And furthermore, since he taught regarding the High Priest [both] "he judges" and "others judge him," he taught regarding the king both "he does not judge" and "others do not judge him." For so too he teaches "others testify against him" regarding the High Priest, and "others do not testify [against him]" regarding the king, even though they are not needed, since they are [already] included in "others judge him"; rather, because he taught regarding "he judges" [also] "others judge him," he likewise taught "he testifies" and "others testify [against him]." And as for the fact that the Talmud does not deliberate like this [concerning the king], it is because this is obvious, that he taught in the latter clause alongside the first clause. So I found in an explanation, [citing] Harav R. [of] Troyes in his name. Yet unnecessarily did he strain to make this precise distinction; for certainly, always, whether regarding a king or regarding a High Priest, if there is a novelty either from "he judges" or from "others judge him," there is no question to be raised whatsoever: "Why did he need to teach regarding the High Priest 'others judge him,' and regarding the king 'he does not judge'?" For once there is any novelty in his statement, he teaches this [clause] alongside that [clause]. And you may know [that this is so], for it is obvious like this to the Talmud, which asks here: "[Isn't that] obvious?" — that is to say: Why do we need to teach "he judges"? And it answers: It was necessary [to teach] "others judge him," and alongside "others judge him" he teaches "he judges." Even so, one cannot ask: Why did [the Gemara] not answer that it was for this reason that he taught [both] "he judges" and "others judge him" — because if he had not taught anything at all, it would have entered your mind [to think] that others do not judge him, and consequently he does not judge on account of "Gather yourselves together"? For on the contrary, to the other side: had he not taught anything regarding the High Priest, I would have said through logic that he certainly judges, for is it so that on account of his importance he is diminished?! And since he judges, we also judge him on account of "Gather yourselves together" — and there is no difficulty at all.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:3:1.hebrew: נמצאו דייני ישראל ז' ריבואות וח' אלפים ושש מאות - תימה: הא חסרי להו טובא! דכי מפקת מס' ריבואות ששה מאות לשרי אלפים, לא משכחת בתר הכי ו' אלפים לשרי מאות; וכי הדר מפקת (כל) הני, לא משכחת בתר הכי לשרי חמשים י"ב אלף; וכ"ש דלא משכחת בתר הכי שרי עשרות שש ריבואות! וי"מ, דבכל הני שרים אפשר דהוו זקנים יתירים מבני ס' — דאמר ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכא:) דלא נמנו פחות מבני עשרים ויתירים מבני ששים. ובשרי עשרות לא חיישינן, אפילו היו מבני עשרים — שהם עצמם היו מן החשבון, וכל אחד שר על תשעה והוא עשירי. וי"מ, דחשבון השררות קחשיב: דתחילתן נימנו שרי עשרות, ומהחשובין שבהם נתמנו לשרי חמשים, והחשובין משרי חמשים נתמנו לשרי מאות, ומשרי מאות בירר החשובים לשרי אלפים:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:3:1.english: "The judges of Israel are found [to be] 78,600" - [This is] astonishing, for they fall short by a great deal! For when you deduct 600 for ministers of thousands from the 600,000, you will not find 6,000 for ministers of hundreds after that; and when you then further deduct all of these, you will not find 12,000 for ministers of fifties after that; and all the more so, you will not find 60,000 ministers of tens after that! And some explain that regarding all these ministers, it is possible that they were elders over sixty years of age — as [the Gemara] states in [the chapter entitled] Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 121b) that [those] under twenty years of age and over sixty years of age were not counted [in the census]. And regarding the ministers of tens, we are not concerned even if they were from [those aged] twenty [to sixty], because they themselves were [included] in the count, and each one was a minister over nine, and he was the tenth. And some explain that it calculates the count of appointments: for at first they were appointed as ministers of tens, and the most prominent among them were appointed as ministers of fifties, and the most prominent of the ministers of fifties were appointed as ministers of hundreds, and from the ministers of hundreds he selected the prominent ones as ministers of thousands.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:5:1.hebrew: והא דתנן כהן גדול בתר פ"ק - משום דאיידי דתניא בפ"ק מילי דכ"ג, פסיק ושיירי ליה; והדר תני ליה מעלות של מלך דחשיב מיניה; ואחר כך חוזר לעניינו — להלכות דינין:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 18a:5:1.english: And that which we learned [the chapter of] "The High Priest" after the first chapter - [It is] because, since in the first chapter matters of the High Priest were taught, [the Tanna] paused [the main topic of court procedure] to address the remaining matters concerning him; and then he taught the prerogatives of the king, who is [even] more distinguished than him; and afterwards he returns to his [primary] subject — to the laws of judgments.
